 Flamengo welcomed Athletico Paranaense to the Maracana on Wednesday, November 18, for a crucial Brazilian Serie A encounter in the 35th round. Leonardo Jardim's league leaders sought to strengthen their championship position, while Odair Hellmann's fifth-placed visitors aimed to end a four-match winless run and improve their chances of qualifying for the Copa Libertadores.
 According to ge.globo, kickoff was scheduled for 8:30 p.m. Brasilia time, with Premiere and sportv broadcasting the match live. Flamengo entered the fixture three points ahead of Palmeiras, with four rounds remaining in the championship.

 Flamengo had recorded three consecutive league victories following their Copa Libertadores elimination against Estudiantes. According to Goal.com, the club had also collected four wins in its previous five Serie A matches, including victories over Gremio and Vasco da Gama.

 The result carried additional importance because Flamengo faced Palmeiras in the following round. A victory would strengthen their position ahead of that direct championship confrontation.
 Flamengo midfielder Bruno Henrique emphasized the team's determination during a club ceremony on November 15, where he and Giorgian de Arrascaeta received special recognition.
 "We know there is not much left before the year ends, there are four games, so we will give everything in these games to win the title. God willing, we can celebrate in December as well," Bruno Henrique said.

 According to Sports Mole, Flamengo had several international players returning before the match. Guillermo Varela, Giorgian de Arrascaeta and Gonzalo Plata were among those who rejoined the squad, while Alex Sandro, Lucas Paqueta and Danilo also resumed group training.
 However, Nicolas de la Cruz and Anthony Valencia were unavailable because of international commitments. Paqueta was still recovering from a knee problem, while Danilo continued rehabilitation following a jaw fracture.
 Eight Flamengo players were also at risk of suspension for the Palmeiras fixture after accumulating yellow cards. The players were Arrascaeta, Pedro, Erick Pulgar, Leo Pereira, Alex Sandro, Bruno Henrique, Luiz Araujo and Vitao.
 Also Read 
 John Daly Reveals 1.65 Million Dollar Gambling Loss 
 Athletico Paranaense arrived with a considerably shorter list of available options. According to Sports Mole, Kevin Viveros, the competition's leading scorer with 21 goals, received an extended three-match suspension following his dismissal against Vasco on November 4.
 The Brazilian sports tribunal extended his punishment during a November 16 hearing. Consequently, Viveros was expected to miss the remaining fixtures until the final round against Sao Paulo.
 Ge.globo also identified defender Arthur Dias and midfielder Luiz Gustavo among the team's absentees. Dantas was suspended after receiving his third yellow card, while Teran and Claudinho were unavailable for contractual and injury-related reasons, respectively.

 Viveros' absence forced Hellmann to consider alternative attacking arrangements, with Kerwin Vargas among the potential replacements. Bruno Zapelli and Portilla were also expected to feature as the coach considered adjustments to his formation.
 Despite their recent difficulties, Athletico remained fifth with 54 points. The club was competing for a place in next season's Copa Libertadores, with Fluminense, Bahia and Atletico Mineiro also involved in the battle for continental qualification.
 Sports Mole reported that Athletico had also received an increased fine of R$30,000 following racist gestures attributed to a supporter during the match against Vasco. The punishment was approved by a majority vote at the November 16 hearing.

 Referee Rafael Rodrigo Klein, representing Rio Grande do Sul, was appointed to oversee the Flamengo-Athletico encounter. Guilherme Dias Camilo and Tiago Augusto Kappes Diel were named as assistant referees, Roger Goulart as fourth official and Caio Max Augusto Vieira as VAR.
